- Overestimate prices in early forecast windows when sentiment is bullish (high sentiment scores) — reduce initial forecast slightly.
- Underestimate late-period spikes (especially >85) when sentiment turns neutral or negative — add a buffer or upward adjustment for momentum.
- When sentiment shows strong reversal (e.g., 0.00–0.20) after a spike, model tends to overcorrect — forecast should lag slightly to avoid premature peak.
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- Overshoot after sentiment spikes: if sentiment >0.75 and price rises >5% from prior, cap forecast at +3–5% above prior to avoid overcorrection.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts often overestimate early period (first 10 days) — adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
